subject: I am in trouble! Is my data lost? ... musings on shinyApps instances and persistent data storage ...

messages.author: da8c498bae447460
messages.subject: I am in trouble! Is my data lost? ... musings on shinyApps instances and persistent data storage ...
parts:
I might have screwed up here :-( ... but perhaps not?

I'm using SQLite as a data repository -- the SQLite file (data.db) is stored locally (on the shinyapps.io server) along with server.R and ui.R

Importantly, my shinyapp reads and writes to the SQLIte database.

All is well, on the face of it: When my shinyapp modifies the data (based on user input), those changes are reflected in the shinyapp output

However, when I download a copy (Bundle) from the shinayapps.io dashboard and look closely at the database file ... no changes appear to have been committed.

I am thinking this has to do with the manner in which application instances are handled by the shinyapps.io server (see this link)

Now to the questions:

1) Am I right, when I suspect the changes to the database only 'live' in a running instance of my shinyapp and will disappear when that instance is terminated?
2) If so, how can I salvage the data.db from that instance?
3) Or am I wrong, and will the changes be transferred from the running instance to the data.db file, so that I might download it?

Kind regards
Soren - Denmark

Soren,
Unfortunately you are in trouble because you do need to treat the storage on shinyapps.io as transient at this time.  We tried to document that in a few places, but perhaps we need to do a better job of making that clear.  

-Tareef

I would suggest a change to this webpage: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/persistent-data-storage.html

I have posted it as a comment on the page itself


Local vs remote storage

Before diving into the different storage methods, one important distinction to understand is local storage vs remote storage.

Local storage means saving a file on the same machine that is running the Shiny application. Functions like write.csv(), write.table(), and saveRDS() implement local storage because they will save a file on the machine running the app. Local storage is generally faster than remote storage, but it should only be used if you always have access to the machine that saves the files. Files store locally on an application instance running on shinyapps.io will only exist within in data space of that instance, and thus only for as long as the instance is running -- once the instance is stopped, the locally stored data is lost!

Remote storage means saving data on another server, usually a reliable hosted server such as Dropbox, Amazon, or a hosted database. One big advantage of using hosted remote storage solutions is that they are much more reliable and can generally be more trusted to keep your data alive and not corrupted.

When going through the different storage type options below, keep in mind that if your Shiny app is hosted on shinyapps.io, you will have to use a remote storage method for the time being. RStudio plans to implement persistent storage on shinyapps.io soon. In the meantime, using local storage is only an option if you’re hosting your own Shiny Server, though that comes at the price of having to manage a server and should only be done if you’re comfortable with administering a server.
